title: 3rd Sitting of third session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened with the agenda and the Speaker's announcements: a committee seat swap, a 20 October deadline for the committee reviewing the Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation nominee, and a presidential letter on the Optional Protocol to the disability rights convention, which was sent to the Foreign Relations Committee. Almost all the time went on debating the government's Proceeds of Crime bill, sponsored by the member for Central Fuvahmulah. PNC members backed it as a tool against corruption, while MDP members raised concerns about wide seizure powers, third-party rights, timing and whether it would be enforced. Debate did not finish before time ran out, and a Criminal Procedure Act amendment bill was put off because nobody asked to speak. The text is partly garbled, so some speaker gists are approximate.

items.title: Opening of the sitting and prayer
Attendance of members

items.title: Debate on the Proceeds of Crime bill (sponsor: Ali Fazad, Central Fuvahmulah, for the government)
items.outcome: debated, 16 speaking turns by 14 members; not concluded, continues at a later sitting

items.title: Debate on the bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act (2016/12) (sponsor: Mohamed Mamdooh, Funadhoo)
items.outcome: deferred, nobody asked to speak; to be put on a later agenda

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the bill so wrongly gained assets can be returned to the state and to people harmed.
Criticised MDP-era deals such as the Noomadi resort compensation and airport board, and defended the government's record on debt and projects.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Called it a blackmail bill because of its timing after an adviser's resignation and said it targets businesspeople.
Argued the bill serves politics ahead of the 2028 election and would breach basic rights.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Backed the bill, saying past governments all faced claims of state funds being misused and nobody should be exempt from action under it.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Backed the bill and cited Quran and hadith teachings against unlawfully earned wealth, bribery and fraud.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised a point of order that the previous speaker was straying from the bill's subject into attacks on the MDP; the chair accepted it.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Called the bill important but noted anti-graft laws already exist and Maldives ranks 93rd of 182 on the corruption index.
Stressed protecting the property rights of people whose assets are held, and said institutions like the Anti-Corruption Commission must actually function.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Welcomed the bill but flagged concerns that clauses 74 and 75 allow seizure of a suspect's whole property, including where the suspect has died or fled.
Said the committee stage should address these concerns and the fair treatment of those affected.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Backed the bill and responded to the MDP leader by recounting the Noomadi dispute and past loan-approval rules; also defended the Rasmale project.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Supported the bill, saying similar laws exist in the UK, US and Singapore and it is not aimed at political opponents; cited an audit report on Addu hospital purchases.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Cited Article 40 of the Constitution on property rights and argued the bill sets court-controlled rules for holding property; supported it as a tool against drug and laundering proceeds.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said the bill is not aimed at any one group and that existing laws lack the detail needed to recover illegally gained assets; supported it.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Said the problem is weak institutions, not missing laws, noting Anti-Corruption Commission case outcomes are not published; saw the bill as comprehensive and left details to committee.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Raised a point of order that the bill was sent to the Majlis before the adviser's resignation, disputing the previous speaker's claim.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said such a law should follow UNCAC and FATF standards but argued the money laundering definition is too broad and third-party rights are unclear.
Doubted the bill could be enforced as drafted, giving small tax and theft cases as examples.

decisions: Ibrahim Nazil replaced Hussain Ziyad on the Economic Affairs Committee for the MDP.
20 October 2026 announced as the committee deadline on the Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation nominee.
The President's letter on the Optional Protocol to the disability rights convention was sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
Debate on the Proceeds of Crime bill was not concluded and continues at a later sitting.
The Criminal Procedure Act amendment bill was deferred because nobody asked to speak.
Next sitting set for Monday 12 October 2026 at 09:00.
